summary: Mihai Șora was a philosopher who studied at the University of Bucharest under Mircea Eliade (~1934–1938), the University of Paris (~1938–1940), and the CNRS (~1945–1948). He held a post at the State Publishing House for Literature and Arts (~1959–1969).
Mihail Alekseevič Širjaev was an Indologist who studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy and Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov. He served as Docent of Indology at the Leningrad Oriental Institute (~1928–1938).

Mihail Nikolaevič Sotnikov worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as Docent of Indology at Leningrad Oriental Institute, Head of Department of Indian Linguistics at MGIMO (1954–1956), and held a post at Moscow State University (1956–1965).

Mikael Aktor specializes in religious studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of Copenhagen in 1998 and became an Associate Professor at the University of Southern Denmark in 1999.

Mikaël Bauer specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Kanazawa University under Paul Hoornaert and Noritoshi Aramaki, and earned his PhD at Harvard under Ryuichi Abe (attested 2010). In 2026, he is attested at McGill University.

Mikel Burley works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Essex under J. M. Bernstein and earned his PhD at Bristol (-2005) under John Peacock. Between 2007 and 2020, he was Associate Professor at the University of Leeds.

Mikhail Izrailevich Tubyansky worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Theodore Stcherbatsky and Boris Vladimirtsov (~1914–1919), and held posts (1920–1937) at the Asiatic Museum, IOM RAS, and Leningrad Institute of Living Oriental Languages.

Mikhail Kudryavtsev was an Indologist who studied at Leningrad Topographical Technical School (1929–1932) and Saint Petersburg State University (~1934–1939). He worked at the Institute of Ethnography as a naučnyj sotrudnik in 1948 and staršij n. sotrudnik in 1969.

Mikhail Nikolayevich Peterson worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Moscow State University (-1913) under Filipp Fortunatov, Nikolai Trubetzkoy, and Wiktor Jan Porzeziński, later serving there as Docent from 1916 to 1952.
Mikhail Pokrovsky studied under Vsevolod Miller and Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov from circa 1888 to 1891.

Mikhail Sergeevich Troitsky worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences (1928–1931) and held a post at the University of Chicago.
Mikhaïl Peterson studied under Wiktor Jan Porzeziński (~1904–1913) and Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov (~1904–1914), and he taught Pavel Grintser and Vyacheslav Ivanov.
Mikio Otsuki works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. In 2007, he is attested as a research fellow at Manpuku-ji and as a professor at Hanazono University.

Mikisaburo Mori was a scholar of philosophy and sinology. He studied at Kyoto University and Osaka University, and held posts at Kyoto University, Osaka High School, Osaka University (Associate Professor 1950, Professor 1966–1973), and Bukkyo University (Professor ~1973–1983).

Mikołaj Kruszewski was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Warsaw and Kazan State University under Jan Niecisław Baudouin de Courtenay, later holding various posts at Kazan State University, including professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Grammar (1885–1886).

Mikołaj Rudnicki worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Jan Michał Rozwadowski at Jagiellonian University (~1903–1911) and served as Professor of Indo-European Linguistics at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań from 1919 to 1950.
Mildred Archer was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. She studied at St Hilda's College, Oxford (~1931–1977) and served as Keeper of Prints and Drawings at the India Office from 1954 to 1980.

Milena Hübschmannová was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Charles University (1951–1956, Ph.D. ~1951–1995). She worked at the Oriental Institute, Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences, a Prague language school, and became Professor of Romani at Charles University in 1991.
Miles Bronson was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Colgate University and Colgate Rochester Crozer Divinity School (~1834–1836). In 1837, he founded the American Baptist Missionary Union.
Milman Parry worked in linguistics. He studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Paris under Antoine Meillet, and he later held a post at Harvard University (~1929–1935).
